name: Dynamic Neural Retraining System (DNRS)
founded_year_range: 2008 (founder bio page on the site); book Wired for Healing 2014; DNRS 2.0 relaunch ~2022
cost_summary: USD (site, Oct 2026): DNRS 2.0 video program $349.95 with 1 year of streaming access, then $20/mo. Jump Start bundle (adds a 60-min coaching session) $439.95. Support bundle (adds 12-wk group coaching, 6 mo of Share-A-Laugh classes and premium forum access) $569.95. Printed package $105.95. Wired for Healing book $24.95. 21-day free trial. Refund only after 6 months of daily practice, less a 15% fee, and within 365 days of purchase.
mechanisms: limbic system impairment / amygdala threat conditioning
autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
mechanism_summary: The program proposes 'limbic system impairment'. A trauma (chemical or toxic exposure, infection, injury, psychological trauma or cumulative stress) 'cross-wires' the brain's threat circuitry and leaves it stuck in a conditioned fight/flight/freeze state through maladaptive neuroplasticity. Benign stimuli (odours, foods, EMFs, exertion, body sensations) are then misread as dangers, producing real symptoms via central sensitisation and a chronic stress response, sustained by hypervigilance and avoidance. Recovery is framed as rewiring this circuitry through daily practice that interrupts threat patterns and rehearses elevated positive states. The same mechanism applies to every condition; only the personal triggers differ.
techniques: ~13 h of streamed video psychoeducation on neuroplasticity and the limbic system ('Five Pillars of Recovery')
daily retraining practice for >=6 months (historically ~1 h/day of 'rounds', per secondary accounts)
pattern interruption of trigger-, symptom- or threat-driven thoughts
visualisation of positive memories and future wellness with elevated emotion
incremental training (graded exposure to avoided triggers such as scents, foods, environments, activity)
emotional and cognitive restructuring; limiting symptom talk and monitoring
1:1 and 12-week group coaching by DNRS-certified coaches
mainstream_notes: No guideline endorsement (NICE, CDC). Referrals come mainly from individual environmental, integrative, functional and mould/CIRS-oriented physicians; Neil Nathan claims to have used it with 'well over a thousand patients' over 15 years. The site claims '>1,000 doctors refer' (unverified). A University of Alberta-sponsored RCT (MILES, NCT06933173) began in July 2025. The program is mentioned in passing in MCS (Jacques 2024) and ME/CFS/long-COVID (Tate 2023) reviews.
insurance_notes: Sold direct to consumers. The site does not mention insurance or HSA/FSA, and coaches are DNRS-certified rather than licensed clinicians, so no reimbursement pathway exists.

key_trials.citation: Guenter D et al. 'Neuroplasticity-based treatment for fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue and multiple chemical sensitivity: feasibility and outcomes' (McMaster University; enrolled 2016). The DNRS site cites it as 2019 with no journal. No PubMed/Europe PMC record; Jacques 2024 calls it unpublished.
key_trials.design: Uncontrolled 12-month observational cohort of DNRS seminar attendees (assessed at 3, 6 and 12 mo)
key_trials.finding: Per the company site: all 8 SF-36 domains improved. Proportions above caseness fell for FM (76.9->26.7%), CFS (71.7->28.6%), MCS (38.9->6.3%), anxiety (48.4->6.5%) and depression (48.4->12.9%). No control group, self-selected paying sample, attrition not reported.

key_trials.citation: MILES: Mind-Body in Long COVID and Myalgic Encephalomyelitis Study, NCT06933173 (PIs Vohra S, Univ. of Alberta, and Stein E, Univ. of Calgary; sponsor University of Alberta), recruiting since 2025-07-10
key_trials.design: RCT, DNRS (14-h online course + 12-wk online group support) vs 4-month wait-list/usual care with crossover; investigator- and assessor-masked; primary outcome SF-36 physical functioning; ME/CFS
key_trials.finding: Ongoing; primary completion est. Dec 2027. No results.

key_trials.citation: DNRS 2025 Client Experiences & Outcomes Survey (company-run, not peer-reviewed)
key_trials.design: Voluntary cross-sectional self-report survey of Global Community Forum members
key_trials.finding: 83.5-95.2% reported some improvement across six domains (physical 89.4%, emotional 95.2%, QoL 94.2%). 19.3-37.6% reported 'significant/life-changing' improvement. No denominator or control group.

key_trials.citation: Toussaint LL, Whipple MO, Abboud LL, Vincent A, Wahner-Roedler DL. 2012, Explore 8(2):92-98, PMID 22385563. NOT DNRS: it tests Gupta 'amygdala retraining' and is listed for disambiguation.
key_trials.design: Single-blind RCT at the Mayo Clinic: standard care + amygdala retraining (2.5-h course, home video) vs standard care, in FM/CFS
key_trials.finding: Only 21 completed (7 intervention, 14 control). Reported significant improvements in physical health, energy, pain, symptom distress and fatigue. High attrition. Tests a different branded program.

controversy: Criticised by ME/CFS advocates (alongside Gupta and the Lightning Process) for psychologising biomedical illness, discouraging symptom talk, risking post-exertional malaise through incremental exertion, and implying that non-recovery reflects insufficient practice; the refund requires 6 months of daily practice. Marketing relies on testimonials, physician endorsements, a self-selected survey and an unpublished uncontrolled cohort, and uses the non-established construct 'limbic system impairment'. The founder lists no clinical degrees or licence. Some ex-participants describe enforced positivity. Others, especially with MCS or mould-related sensitivity, report major recovery. The MILES PIs also co-authored a 2021 mind-body ME/CFS review, and co-PI Stein is reported to favour brain-retraining approaches (not re-verified).

indicators.metric: Wired for Healing copies sold (company claim)
Patients referred by a single endorsing physician (Neil Nathan)

popularity.reach_estimate: ~30k-100k cumulative participants (tens of thousands of course purchasers, plus 65k+ book buyers, some overlapping). The site claims it has 'helped thousands'.
popularity.method_notes: Web-search quota was exhausted in both the research and fact-check runs, so Google Trends, Reddit subscriber counts and YouTube metrics could not be retrieved. The trajectory is anchored on documented milestones: 2008 launch (founder page), 2014 book with a claimed 65k+ sales, 2016 McMaster seminar cohort, functional-medicine/mould-community uptake ~2016-2019 (Nathan endorsement), the 2020-22 shift online and long-COVID surge with the DNRS 2.0 relaunch (~2022), and the 2025 client survey and MILES RCT start. Levels are judgement-based within-program relative scores. The reach estimate is triangulated from company claims (book sales, 'thousands helped') and single-physician referral counts, all unaudited.
